round_1.verdict_reason: The correction, its activation gate, undo and derive_segment_angles are correct, but the AB04/i0 account omits the pelvis and segment angular velocities. These are standardized features that the UM21 producers compute from the stored (reversed) pelvis. The hook does not govern them, so an adapter that follows the handoff rule would publish them wrong for AB04/i0.

checks.evidence: rec4 multiplier +1 and rec1 multiplier -1, so both publish the rule-B truth bit for bit. Independent reasoning: corrected clinical tilt = -stored, and rule B = -clinical, so +stored. Matches UM21-P01 (flipped residual 0.13-0.15 deg).

checks.evidence: write_json_exclusive then undo with expected_log_sha256 restores stored arrays bit for bit. A wrong digest raises UndoError, and a log with the multiplier tampered to -1 raises UndoError.

checks.evidence: Real table with an activated backlog copy. AB04/i00, AB40/i0, AB04/d0, AB04/i1 and AB14/i0 run without a correction, so their reversed tilt is held by the detector rule. ab04/i0, 'AB04/i0\n', ' AB04/i0' and 'AB04\i0' raise on the id pattern. Recording membership is exact list membership.

checks.claim: Inactive unless UM21-P01/P02 are done and cite the id and the decision answer is exactly C
checks.evidence: Decision answers 'c', 'C ', 'B', None and 'defer' each hold the tilt, returned as stored. The committed backlog (UM21-P02 status 'ready') holds, with the reason naming UM21-P02. Both backlog records cite UM21-P01-AB04-i0-pelvis as a whole token.

checks.claim: A correction listed for a normally stored recording does not publish a flipped tilt
checks.evidence: Normal storage under an active correction: the detector suggests the opposite sign, the tilt is held and returned uncorrected (applied false), and derive_segment_angles derives nothing.

Independent 2-D geometry, 1000 random poses: with CCW segment angles (thigh/shank zero vertical with the distal end down, foot zero forward horizontal), hip flexion, knee flexion and ankle dorsiflexion measured in their named directions satisfy thigh = pelvis + hip, shank = thigh - knee and foot = shank + ankle exactly. A top-of-pelvis-forward tilt measures negative. foot = shank + ankle matches the reference table row (up to zero offsets).

checks.claim: Passed-in segment angles for AB04/i0 are held, never flipped
checks.evidence: The MATLAB producers build thigh, shank and foot from the stored pelvis (time converter after choose_pelvis_signal; phase converter 'enforces hip = thigh - pelvis' block). Flipping them would not fix them, because the error is additive: 2 x tilt. Holding them and recomputing from published channels is right. derive_segment_angles ignores every SEGMENT_CHANNELS input.

findings.finding: The AB04/i0 account omits pelvis and segment angular velocities.
detail: convert_umich_time_to_parquet.m computes pelvis_sag_vel and right/left thigh/shank/foot velocities as gradients of the stored pelvis and of the segments built from it. convert_umich_phase_to_parquet.m computes thigh/shank/foot velocities from segments built on the stored pelvis.

For AB04/i0 the effects are: pelvis sagittal velocity is sign-flipped; pelvis frontal velocity is sign-flipped; pelvis transverse velocity crosses the +/-180 deg wrap (heading about +/-179.77 deg), so its gradient can spike; and segment velocities carry 2 x d(tilt)/dt.
The hook has no velocity channels and no not_released or derived entry naming them. The handoff adapter rule mentions only segment angles.
requested_fix: Extend the AB04/i0 exception and the handoff adapter rule.

Pelvis sagittal velocity and thigh/shank/foot velocities must be recomputed after the hook from the published and derived angles, with the dataset's documented derivative method, or else not released for AB04/i0.
Pelvis frontal and transverse velocities must be listed as not released, alongside obliquity and rotation.
Add a test that the table names them.
No hook logic change is needed unless the worker chooses to validate velocity names.

findings.finding: The UM21 MATLAB producers are a blocker for any UM21 full run unless the adapter computes segment angles and their velocities after the hook.
detail: The fail-safe holds AB04/i0 segment-angle inputs, so no wrong angle can publish. No equivalent fail-safe exists for velocities.
For all recordings, segment angles and velocities follow the pre-rule-B recipe.
No CORE-11-P-UM21 task exists in the backlog yet. Its acceptance criteria must require derive_segment_angles plus post-hook velocity derivation, or a producer fix.

checks.claim: Velocity coverage is complete against the UM21 standardized features
evidence: feature_constants.SEGMENT_VELOCITY_FEATURES lists pelvis sagittal/frontal/transverse and thigh/shank/foot sagittal ipsi/contra.
Pelvis sagittal and thigh/shank/foot velocities appear in derived_velocities, with the column mapping in velocity_rule. Ipsi and contra come from the per-leg hook runs.
Pelvis frontal and transverse velocities are in not_released.
Trunk velocities: UM21 producers emit no trunk or thorax. Joint velocities (hip, knee, ankle) are unaffected by the pelvis reversal.
The producers compute pelvis_sag_vel but do not write a pelvis velocity column; covered anyway.
The hook refuses an incomplete derived_velocities (malformed-correction tests: missing foot velocity; None).

checks.claim: derive_angular_velocities equals MATLAB gradient as used by the UM21 converters
checks.result: pass (against MATLAB's documented algorithm; MATLAB itself not run)
evidence: Independent hand-written MATLAB gradient was used: interior (F(i+1)-F(i-1))/(2h), one-sided first and last samples.

Five units with different per-unit stride durations (h = duration/149), with NaN at the first, middle, last and three consecutive samples: max relative difference 0 versus gradient(F, h) and 2.2e-16 versus the converters' gradient(F)*effective_Hz. NaN patterns are identical: a NaN sample's own velocity stays finite and its neighbours become NaN, as in MATLAB.
Time series with scalar dt: difference 0.
A spacing vector of the wrong length raises.
Spacing is uniform within each unit in both converters (time: dt = 1/sampling_rate_hz on a resampled grid; phase: 150 points per stride), so MATLAB's nonuniform-coordinate formula never applies.

checks.claim: Holding every *_velocity channel cannot break anything that should publish
evidence: The detector consumes no velocity channels; velocity appears only in the power description text.
Adding hip and knee velocity inputs to a normal recording leaves every other channel's publication, multiplier and votes unchanged.
No audited-sign entry names a velocity.
The only other caller (core11_gt21_publication_effect.py) passes no velocities.

Velocity-like names without the _velocity suffix (pelvis_sagittal_velocity_rad_s, thigh_sagittal_velocity_ipsi_rad_s, pelvis_tilt_vel, *_omega, *_rate, upper case) still hold, through abstain with no audit, on both the corrected and a normal recording. They are safe, but the hold reason is generic.

The known-value test covers ramp slopes including the ends, a quadratic's interior and one-sided ends, per-unit stride spacing and invalid spacings.
The committed-table test checks derived_velocities, not_released and velocity_rule.
